## State shape and where its migration runs

```
ch.armorWear   { armorEntryKey: DR points lost }   new
ch.armorGuard  { armorEntryKey: true }             new, the repair quality edge
ch.shieldWear  { shieldEntryKey: boxesMarked }     converted from a NAME key (closes L7)
```

Declared in `blank()` at `app/js/store.js:129-132`. The catalog `dr` is the BASE and the ceiling; **absent means undamaged**, which is what delivers "a re-acquired piece arrives fresh" with no heuristic, the same way `ch.rig.hp` does.

I named it `armorWear`, not `ch.armorDR` as `DEFERRED-FIXES.md` sketched. A map called `armorDR` either holds a number that is not the DR, or holds the current value and so duplicates the catalog on every acquisition and must be written for pieces nobody has touched. Wear also makes it and `shieldWear` one shape, which was the whole argument for doing them together.

**Migration** is one shared block in `migrate()`, immediately after the `ch.rig` block and therefore after the instance-id split, per the ordering rule recorded at the split. The pre-split `shieldWear` normalization at the old `:213-214` is deleted and replaced with a pointer comment.

## shieldWear's migration, per old shape

One rule for all three maps: **a key that already names a live entry is kept; a key that names an owned item's NAME becomes that item's first owned entry; anything else is dropped.** The live-entry test runs first, which is what makes it idempotent (after one pass the keys are ids, and an id-keyed map is indistinguishable from a name-keyed one except by asking the equipment list) and what keeps a legitimately name-keyed pooled row working. Two keys resolving to one entry keep the first and drop the second. All three maps are rebuilt null-prototype.

Seven import shapes, each re-loaded twice: zero throws, all seven byte-stable across three loads. `{"Scrap Shield":2,"Riot Shield":1}` lands on the first owned entry of each name with the second Anvil Frame left untouched at 5/5; a name nothing owns is dropped; junk values, non-object maps, absent fields and prototype-name keys all normalize to `{}`.

## Every reader of armor DR

`EN.engine.armorState(ch, key)` is the resolver. `defensiveLoadout` sets `armorDR` from `armorState().current` and publishes `armorBaseDR / armorDRLost / armorBreached / armorGuard / armorState / armorKey / shieldKey` on `d.defenseGear`, so `d.armorDR` and `d.totalDR` are current by construction. That covers the DR stat tile, the DR breakdown, the Block tray's flat row, the Block summary, and the Plated half-DR term. Individually updated: the Freelancer gear chip (`3 of 5 DR`), the DR breakdown row and footer, the stash item card (per entry), the print sheet stat tile and inventory line (`DR 1 of 3 (2 lost, until repaired)`), the PDF DR field and inventory notes (confirmed by instrumenting `armorState` during a real `EN.pdfExport.build`: `eq_b1->1/3`). The Impact Table's mod-bench header keeps the catalog base and now says `5 BASE DR`, because that panel is keyed on the armor TYPE (`ch.armorMods` is name-keyed).

One behaviour change worth flagging: a lapsed lease now grants `min(lapsedDR, current)`, so a breached Sentinel Issue grants 0 instead of falling back up to its `lapsedDR` of 1.

**I also found and fixed a defect in my own work**: for part of the build there were two writers, and the Impact Table's ignored the quality guard, burning a point the Defenses row would have absorbed. Collapsed to `EN.engine.applyArmorDamage(c, key, delta)`, the one writer, which clamps to `[0, base]` in both directions and spends the guard.

Numbers live in `EN.crafting.armorRepair`. Shop: 10 percent of list per point, one Downtime period, no roll, pays on the spot. Bench: 5 percent per point in parts, opened as a Simple Engineering Project that rolls, salvages, secures and completes like any other; a `Portable Fabrication Rig` makes parts free. At 0 DR it is not a repair: it routes to an ordinary Project at the item's own tier and full parts cost. Measured on an Anvil Frame (list 920, base 5): 2 points shop `𝒢184` / bench `𝒢92`, full 5 points shop `𝒢460`, which is half of 920 and reproduces the manuscript's own rate derivation.

`tbStart` carries `repairKey` and `repairPoints`; `tbComplete` pays out through the one writer, so a Project cannot exceed the base and one whose piece left the stash restores nothing (`PIECE GONE` chip). A log containing a Flawless interval sets `armorGuard`.

## F1. A shield announces its own destruction one box early. In-app, no import. CONFIRMED LIVE.

`app/js/combat.js:3490`

```js
store.update(function (c) {
  c.shieldWear = c.shieldWear || {};
  var n = eng.clamp((c.shieldWear[key] | 0) + delta, 0, max);
  if (n > 0) c.shieldWear[key] = n; else delete c.shieldWear[key];
});
var left = Math.max(0, max - eng.clamp((((ch.shieldWear || {})[key] | 0) + delta), 0, max));
```

`ch` is `store.active()` (`app/js/combat.js:1826`) and `store.update` mutates that same object in place, so by line 3490 the stored value **already includes `delta`**. Line 3490 adds it a second time. `left` is therefore one box lower than reality on every wear click.

Driven through the real `− WEAR` button on a Riot Shield (3 boxes), toast captured off the live `#toast` node:

```
click 2:  shieldWear {"eq_sh1":2}   boxesLeft 1   shieldAlive TRUE   blockDie 1d6
          toast: "Riot Shield is destroyed; the wreck is salvage."
click 3:  shieldWear {"eq_sh1":3}   boxesLeft 0   shieldAlive false
          toast: "Riot Shield is destroyed; the wreck is salvage."   (this one is true)
```

The panel simultaneously reads `2/3 left` and the shield keeps granting `+1 DEF` and its `1d6` Block die, so the app contradicts itself on screen in the same frame. The same expression makes it worse for a 2-box shield: on a Scrap Shield the **first** click announces destruction with a box still to spend. Rendering is correct throughout (it reads `dg.shieldBoxesLeft`); only the toast lies, but the toast is the only thing that tells a player the shield is gone.

Root cause is F6: `markShieldWear` re-derives "boxes left" instead of asking the one place that owns the answer.

`app/js/store.js:168` — `if (!ch.proficiencies) return;` (the doc anchors this as `:165`; stale). Every step-5 map is declared at `:129-132` and migrated at `:517-544`, i.e. behind this return, and so is the instance-id split at `:329-442`.

Imported through the real `EN.store.importCharacter`, a record with no `ch.proficiencies`:

      armorWear {"Anvil Frame":3}   shieldWear {"Riot Shield":2}
out:  equipment UNCHANGED - no ids, qty still 2

      shieldWear {"Riot Shield":2} prototype = Object.prototype
      ownedArmorPieces() -> 1 record for 2 suits, key "Anvil Frame"

So for this record: invariant 1 is false (name-keyed), invariant 3 is false (plain prototype), and "two pieces of the same armor hold damage independently" is false — the Impact Table shows one row for two suits, damaging either damages both, and a re-bought Anvil Frame arrives already at 2/5. Mechanism worth recording alongside it: `keyToName` (`app/js/engine.js:873`) returns the key itself when no entry matches, so a name-keyed piece keeps reporting a real base after it leaves the stash — `armorState({equipment:[]}, "Anvil Frame")` returns `base 5, current 3, guard true`. ## F3. Migration does not clamp wear to the piece's capacity, and the first repair after import is paid for and does nothing. Import-only. CONFIRMED LIVE.

`app/js/store.js:541` — `positiveInt` accepts any finite positive number:

```
import armorWear {"eq_o1":999} on an Anvil Frame (base 5)
  -> stored 999 survives migration and every reload
  -> armorState: 0/5, lost 5, breached   (display is correct)
  -> applyArmorDamage(key, -5), which is exactly what tbComplete calls with
     restored = min(repairPoints, st.lost) = 5:
       clamp(999 - 5, 0, 5) = 5   ->  still 0/5, still breached
```

`armorRebuildProject` (`app/js/inventory.js:1758-1770`) passes `repairPoints: st.base` = 5, so a completed full Rebuild Project at full parts cost (𝒢460 on this suit, confirmed debited) restores **zero** DR; the shop lane charges the same 𝒢460 for the same nothing. A second repair then works, because the first one normalized 999 down to 5. `shieldWear` has the identical shape (`{"eq_s1":99}` survives as 99; `+ REPAIR` clamps 98 to 3 and the shield stays destroyed), just with no Glimmer attached. The derived DR never exceeds base or drops below 0 on any path I could find, so the invariant as literally stated survives — but the stored value is out of range and the resolver's clamp is what pays for it. `migrateWearMap` is the natural clamp point and it does not clamp.

## F4. The conversion rule as implemented is "first key in iteration order wins", not "a live entry key is kept". Import-only. CONFIRMED LIVE.

`app/js/store.js:526-539`. The doc and the code comment at `:504-513` both say a key naming a live entry is left alone. Per key that is true; across keys it is not, because the name key can claim the slot first and then `out[key] != null` drops the live one:

```
{"eq_d1":1, "Anvil Frame":4}  ->  {"eq_d1":1}   (live key won, by luck of order)
{"Anvil Frame":4, "eq_d1":1}  ->  {"eq_e1":4}   (stale name key won, live value DROPPED)
{"Riot Shield":2, "eq_s1":1}  ->  {"eq_s1":2}   same, shieldWear
```

Two logically identical records migrate to different numbers depending on JSON key order. Reachable on any half-converted file (hand-merged, or a save exported mid-refactor). Not an identity or clamp violation — invariant 4 is honoured, one value is dropped rather than merged — but the surviving value is arbitrary, and the authoritative one is the one that loses half the time. Fix is one pass ordering: resolve live-entry keys before name keys.

## F5. Invariant 3 is violated at two creation sites, and it is not cosmetic. Exploit is import-only.

`app/js/store.js:129-132` (`blank()`) and `app/js/engine.js:930-931` (`c.armorWear = c.armorWear || {}` / `c.armorGuard = c.armorGuard || {}`) both create **plain** objects. Only `migrateWearMap` builds them null-prototype, and `createAndActivate` (`app/js/store.js:617`) does not call `migrate`, so every character born in-app carries three plain maps until the next page load — and a record that hit F2's early return carries them forever.

Consequence proven on the real functions, with `armorGuard` plain and an entry whose `id` is `"toString"`:

```
armorState(...).guard        -> TRUE, on a suit that was never repaired
applyArmorDamage(+1)         -> absorbed: true, nothing stored
  (the guard "spend" is delete c.armorGuard[key] on an INHERITED property: a no-op)
applyArmorDamage(+1) again   -> absorbed: true.  Forever. The suit cannot lose DR.
same call, null-proto map    -> absorbed: false, armorWear {"toString":1}   (correct)
```

Needs an `e.id` of `toString` / `constructor` / `valueOf` from an import or a hand-edited save — the exact shape the split already null-proto-guards against at `app/js/store.js:357-361`, so the codebase's own standard treats it as real. Non-catalog names cannot reach it (base 0 short-circuits the writer).

## F6. Armor has one resolver. Shields have none.

`EN.engine.armorState` genuinely is the single answer for armor DR, and I verified every consumer reads it or the `d.armorDR` / `d.totalDR` it feeds: DR stat tile, DR breakdown row and footer (`combat.js:1984,1988`), Block tray flat row (`:3525`), Block summary (`:3585`), Plated half-DR (`:3470`), Freelancer gear chip (`:2095`), stash card (`inventory.js:574`). Print sheet and PDF both check out under instrumentation — `["eq_ar1->5/5","eq_ar2->1/5","eq_sh1->0/0","eq_sh2->0/0"]` from each, print sheet rendering `DR 1 · Anvil Frame · 1 of 5` and `1 of 5 (4 lost, until repaired)`; the PDF claim needed `await` to observe (`build` is async) but it holds.

Shields have no such function. `defensiveLoadout` computes `shieldSpent` / `shieldBoxesLeft` inline at `app/js/engine.js:972-977`, and `markShieldWear` computes its own second answer at `app/js/combat.js:3487` and `:3490`. Two derivations, and the second one is wrong — that is F1. Since the whole argument for converting `shieldWear` in this change was that the two mechanics must not diverge, the resolver should have been converted with the key. Two smaller items in the same family: `app/js/inventory.js:2161` writes `c.armorGuard[p.repairKey] = true` outside the one writer (a set, so nothing can diverge arithmetically — a nit); and shield durability appears on **neither** the print sheet nor the PDF, while armor DR is now on both.

## FINDING 1 (substantive) — the bench gate IS a new gate, and it is the only place in the app a Project tier is enforced

`app/data/crafting.js:117` adds `meetsTier`, and `app/js/inventory.js:1778` is its **only** call site in the entire codebase (grep confirms). The app enforces Project tiers nowhere else, so this is not "the existing Project tier requirement doing its job" - it is a brand-new binding check wired to exactly one button. The brief's instruction was "Find where the app enforces Project tiers and let it do its job." There is no such place; `skillTier` was purely decorative (`inventory.js:1939`, "Expects Proficient").

**Failing scenario, verified live.** Character with Engineering `untrained`, two Anvil Frames (list 920, base 5 DR), one at 4/5 and one at 0/5. Rendered Impact Table button states:

Anvil Frame 4/5   SHOP 𝒢92   BENCH 𝒢46  -> disabled
                  "A Simple Project expects Proficient in Engineering; yours is Untrained."
Anvil Frame 0/5   REBUILD PROJECT 𝒢460  -> ENABLED

Clicking REBUILD as that untrained character produced:

The Standard tier's own `skillTier` is `proficient`. The implementer's own note ("Blueprints, custom Projects and the 0 DR rebuild stay advisory as they always were") describes the defect rather than defusing it: when a requirement binds in one mechanic and nowhere else, it is an armor-repair-specific gate regardless of the generic name on the helper.

## What my lens confirmed clean

- **Shop 10 percent per point and bench 5 percent per point are exact.** I ran all 26 armor rows in `EN.gearCatalog.armor` against every DR point 1..base and compared `AR.shopCost` / `AR.benchCost` to exact integer arithmetic (`ceil(p*n/10)`, `ceil(p*n/20)`): **0 mismatches**. No float drift from `Math.ceil` on the `price * 0.10 * points` product.
- **Full re-plate of a 5 DR suit is exactly half list.** Anvil Frame 920 -> 460, Bastion Plate 980 -> 490, Laborframe Exorig 1500 -> 750, Warframe Shell 2400 -> 1200, Bailiff Rig 430 -> 215. The manuscript's own rate derivation reproduces.
- **Bench really is a Simple Engineering Project.** Started one live: `{tier:"simple", target:3, snag:1, skill:"Engineering", materialCost:46, addOnComplete:false, repairKey:"eq_...", repairPoints:1}`. 46 = 5 percent of 920. `addOnComplete:false` means no phantom second suit lands in the Stash.
- **0 DR is genuinely not treated as a repair.** At `lost >= base` the SHOP and BENCH buttons are gone entirely, replaced by `REBUILD PROJECT · 𝒢460` = `materialCost` = half list, at the item's own tier, restoring the full base. (Setting aside Finding 2's pricing basis and Finding 1's missing gate.)
- **Portable Fabrication Rig zeroes bench parts and only bench parts.** With the rig in the Stash the button read `BENCH · PARTS FREE` with a `FAB RIG` chip and `materialCost: 0`; the breached suit's `REBUILD PROJECT · 𝒢460` was unchanged, which is correct - a rebuild is not the bench lane.
- **Salvage still applies to repair Projects.** The card renders `Materials 𝒢92 (repair parts)` with a `SALVAGE` toggle; salvaging then securing spent 𝒢0 and set `materialsSecured: true`.

- `ownsFabRig` (`inventory.js:1704`) grants free parts for merely owning the rig; the manuscript's "with stock on hand" and the item's own "when materials are available" line are not modeled.
- The `↶ UNDO` button restores DR for free with no limit and stays enabled on a breached suit, sitting inches from the priced lanes. It is symmetric with the manual `− DR` button, so it reads as a deliberate tracker affordance rather than a bug.
- The shop lane consumes no calendar time. Nothing else in the app charges a Downtime period either (cipher acquisition says "one Downtime period" and charges only Glimmer), so this is consistent, not a defect.
- Unrelated to my lens: the implementer's report says `.claude/launch.json` was restored to "its committed three entries." It has two, and it is unmodified in `git status`. No harm, but the claim is wrong.

## LENS RESULT: not clean. One confirmed mis-attribution bug in the migration, plus two rules-fidelity gaps.

Ran on my own origin (`http://localhost:8861`, background server, now stopped; `.claude/launch.json` never written by me and byte-identical to my pre-run backup; 8777 untouched; my tab closed; tree still dirty with the same 8 files). I had to close one orphaned tab (`tab-11`, dead port 8813, a previous agent's) to get under the tab cap. Forced reload confirmed fresh code before every reading.

---

### FINDING 1 (CONFIRMED, the one that matters). Name-keyed wear lands on a different piece than the equip slots do

`app/js/store.js:533` resolves a name key through `wearFirstKeyByName`, built at `:519-525` as **the first row in post-split order**. Every other name-keyed map in the same migration (`equippedArmor`, `equippedShield`, `equippedWeapons`, `carry`, `slotInert`, `racked`) resolves through the split's own `firstId(name)` at `:411`. Those two disagree, because `:408`

```js
nameToIds[e.name] = ids;      // ASSIGNS, does not accumulate
```

is executed once per row, so a second id-less row of the same name overwrites the first row's mapping and `firstId()` returns the **last** such row's id.

Failing scenario, reproduced through the real `EN.store.importCharacter` (not my seeding path):

```
equipment: [{name:"Vanguard Plate",qty:1},{name:"Vanguard Plate",qty:1},
            {name:"Scrap Shield",qty:1},{name:"Scrap Shield",qty:1}]
equippedArmor:"Vanguard Plate"   equippedShield:"Scrap Shield"
armorWear:{"Vanguard Plate":3}   shieldWear:{"Scrap Shield":2}
```

after import:

```
equippedArmor  -> eq_k1yfrn6      armorWear  -> {eq_kq7g4yp: 3}
equippedShield -> eq_nla0bpc      shieldWear -> {eq_s8eoxci: 2}
carry          -> {eq_k1yfrn6:"carried"}      <- follows the split, not the wear map

worn suit defends at 4 / 4        stashed spare sits at 1 / 4
wielded shield reads 0 / 2 boxes  stashed spare holds the 2 marked boxes
```

This is exactly the "state parked on the wrong object" failure invariants 1 and 4 exist to prevent, and it lands on the piece the character is actually wearing. It is not the documented per-row hole (that one is `e.id`-carrying rows with `qty > 1`); this one needs **no** ids at all.

Reachability: import and hand-edit only. In-app `addToStash` (`app/js/inventory.js:99-111`) and `builder.js:993` always mint an id for a non-stackable, and the pre-split app pooled duplicates into one `qty:2` row (that shape, `K_pooled`, migrates **correctly** — I verified it). So it is the same reachability class the split's own duplicate-id guard was written for (`store.js:337` says so explicitly), and the migration is precisely the code whose job is import robustness.

Fix is one line and the correct mapping already exists: either make `:408` accumulate (`nameToIds[e.name] = (nameToIds[e.name]||[]).concat(ids)`), or have `migrateWearMap` consult `firstId(name)` before falling back to its own index. Note the pre-existing overwrite also orphans the first row's `carry`/`racked`/equip state, so fixing `:408` fixes both.

### FINDING 2. The tier gate is enforced on the cheap lane and skipped by the stronger lane in the same panel

`app/js/inventory.js:1778` gates BENCH with `meetsTier("simple", …)`. `app/js/inventory.js:1817` REBUILD PROJECT has no check, and it opens a **Standard** Project, which `meetsTier("standard","untrained")` also returns `false` for (`simple->proficient`, `standard->proficient`).

Live, Engineering Untrained: BENCH is `disabled` with the right tooltip and creates nothing, then I clicked `− DR` down to 0/4 and the same panel offered `⚒ REBUILD PROJECT · 𝒢290`, which secured, logged, completed, restored **4 / 4 DR and set `armorGuard`**. So the denial is bypassable inside the panel that issues it, by the destructive button sitting next to it. DEFERRED-FIXES.md:1053-1058 discloses the rebuild as deliberately ungated to match Blueprints, so this is a known scope choice rather than an oversight, but the observable result contradicts "the bench lane is closed to anyone without Engineering Proficiency" and I would not leave it unflagged.

### FINDING 3. Both lanes sell only the whole loss, though the rule prices per point

`app/js/inventory.js:1822`: `var pts = st.lost;`. Live: Vanguard Plate (list 580) at 1/4, Glimmer 100. Only `▤ SHOP · 𝒢174` and `⚒ BENCH · 𝒢87` are offered, shop refuses ("Not enough Glimmer for the shop repair (𝒢174)"), and there is no way to buy back 1 point for 𝒢58 even though the manuscript prices per point of DR restored. Low severity, but it is a rule the UI does not expose.

---

### Reader sweep: CLEAN

`EN.engine.armorState` (`app/js/engine.js:900`) really is the single resolver, and `applyArmorDamage` (`:927`) the single writer (clamps verified with ±99 in both directions; guard spent only on `delta > 0`, never on a repair). Every DR-bearing surface reads current. A Vanguard Plate (base 4) worn at 2 lost, with an undamaged sibling in the stash:

| surface | reads | observed |
|---|---|---|
| `d.armorDR` / `d.totalDR` | `armorState().current` | 2 / 2 |
| Freelancer DR tile | `d.totalDR` | `DR 2 · Vanguard Plate` |
| DR breakdown (tooltip + panel) | `dg.armorDR/BaseDR/DRLost` | `Armor · Vanguard Plate (2 of 4, 2 lost): 2` |
| Freelancer gear chip | `dg.armorDRLost` | title `2 of 4 DR · +1 Block · -1 SPD` |
| Block tray flat row / summary | `d.armorDR` | `to your Armor DR (2)` |
| Plated half-DR | `floor(dg.armorDR/2)` | `+1 half-DR (Plated)` |
| Block tray PLATING row | `dg.armorState` | `2 / 4 DR □□■■` |
| Stash item card | `armorState(ch, ownedKey)` | `⛨ 2 / 4 DR` vs sibling `⛨ 4 DR` |
| Print sheet stat tile | `d.armorDR` | `DR 2 · Vanguard Plate · 2 of 4` |
| Print sheet inventory | `armorState(ch, key)` | `DR 2 of 4 (2 lost, until repaired)` vs sibling `DR 4` |
| PDF stat field + inventory notes | `d.armorDR`, `armorState(ch,key)` | instrumented during a real `EN.pdfExport.build`: `eq_v1->2/4`, `eq_v2->4/4`, 175930 bytes, no throw |
| Impact Table mod-bench header | catalog `dr`, labelled | `MEDIUM ARMOR · 4 BASE DR` |
| Gray Market card | catalog `dr` | base, correct for an unowned item |
| Codex | nothing | zero DR reads in `app/js/codex.js`, confirmed by grep |

Exhaustive `\.dr\b` sweep over `app/**/*.js` leaves only intended base/mod readers: `engine.js:491` and `:776` (lineage natural DR and armor-**mod** flat DR, not piece DR), `engine.js:899` (`armorBaseDR`, base by definition), `inventory.js:579` (market branch), `inventory.js:1869` (mod bench, labelled BASE). No stale name-keyed reader of `shieldWear` survives anywhere.

Lapsed lease is coherent, `min(lapsedDR, current)`, checked at every step on a Bailiff Rig (base 5, lapsedDR 3): undamaged lapsed 3, at 2/5 lapsed 2, breached lapsed 0, paid+breached 0, paid at 2/5 2.

### Migration attack: clean except Finding 1

Ten shapes, seeded and loaded, then persisted and re-loaded twice more. **Zero throws, roster intact, all ten byte-stable across three loads.**

- no DR state at all (fields deleted) -> `{}` each, both null-prototype
- name-keyed `shieldWear` `{"Scrap Shield":2,"Riot Shield":1}` with two Scrap Shields -> `{eq_s1:2, eq_r1:1}`, second Scrap Shield untouched
- `shieldWear`/`armorWear`/`armorGuard` on gear no longer owned -> all dropped, nothing clamped onto another piece
- junk types (`"nope"`, `[1,2,3]`, `7`) -> `{}` each
- junk values (`-2`, `"3"`, `null`, `{}`, `0`, `2.7`, `true`) -> only `2.7 -> 2` survives; `armorGuard` keeps only literal `true`
- prototype-name keys (`constructor`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`) -> dropped, no crash, maps null-prototype
- two keys resolving to one entry -> first kept, second dropped
- `qty:0` row -> dropped
- name key on a `qty:3` no-id row -> first minted id
- `{id:"eq_multi", qty:3}` -> the already-documented per-row hole, unchanged

Two non-findings worth recording rather than raising:

- A non-array `ch.equipment` still throws in `migrate()` and `load()` answers by discarding the **entire roster** (I lost all 9 test characters to it once). Source is pre-existing (`((ch && ch.equipment) || []).forEach` in `ownedRigs`, `engine.js:1126`, present at HEAD); the new blocks correctly use `Array.isArray`. This is DEFERRED L10, not new.
- `engine.js:930-931`, `inventory.js:2161` and `combat.js:3486` create the maps with plain `|| {}` rather than `Object.create(null)`, a deviation from invariant 3. After any load the fields already exist null-prototype so the fallback never fires; only a character created in-session keeps a plain map, and its entry keys can only be `eq_*`. I confirmed a hand-edited `id:"constructor"` armor row behaves correctly after migrate (3/4, guard false, `armorWear:{"constructor":1}`). Hygiene, not a live defect.

End-to-end behaviour I confirmed working: two Anvil-equivalent suits hold damage independently; shop lane charges `580×0.10×pts` (𝒢116 for 2, 𝒢174 for 3) and refuses cleanly when short; bench lane opens `Repair … (+2 DR)` / simple / target 3 / parts 𝒢58 / `addOnComplete:false`, secures, completes, restores to 4/4, adds no duplicate suit, and a Flawless log sets `armorGuard`, which then absorbs exactly one point and is spent; breached suit disables `− DR` and routes `→ REPAIR` to the Impact Table; two Scrap Shields wear independently through the real `− WEAR` button and a destroyed shield drops to `shieldDef 0`; all seven tabs render for four characters with zero console errors.
